title: Xanthe and the Veil Anew
premise: Freya Ravensworth has survived twenty years in the city of Vell by being unremarkable: a royal food-taster whose slow-built immunity to poison is her only magic, and a charm-seller whose wares are harmless enough to escape the outlaw on sorcery. But when prayers start being answered and the old gods stir beneath the mountain, Freya learns her late sister's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain to buy Freya's own survival as a child. To reclaim it, she must gather the found family she never meant to make—a disgraced priest, a god-touched street thief, and her sharp-tongued fellow taster—and trade her hard-won immunity, the one thing keeping her alive, for her sister's freedom. In the end Freya gives up her protection, survives the court's final test through loyalty rather than magic, and returns to a city where the veil between gods and mortals is torn open—and where she finally stops hiding.
about_author: Wendell Lockridge is the pen name of a former line cook who claims the best education in human nature came from feeding people at 2 a.m. He writes fantasy about small magics, large debts, and the families we assemble from strangers. Xanthe and the Veil Anew is his third novel.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A routine morning tasting the king's breakfast turns strange when a dish that should kill her tastes of incense and old stone—prayer, she realizes, is working again. She pockets a silver charm she sold days ago, now warm and humming. Emotional beat: unease; the invisibility she built is cracking.

chapters.title: Charms for a Godless City
chapters.summary: Still Freya's POV, with a flashback to her sister Wren's death twenty years ago. Freya sells charms in the night market and notices customers' wishes coming true in small, terrible ways. The disgraced priest Anselm recognizes her work and warns her: answered prayers have a collector. Emotional beat: dread mixed with longing for the faith she abandoned.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Remembers
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. He takes Freya beneath the city to a sealed shrine where the veil first tore. There she learns the truth: Wren's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain to purchase Freya's poison-immunity—the price of her survival was her sister. Emotional beat: guilt detonating into resolve.

chapters.title: A Thief Who Prays
chapters.summary: New POV: Pip, a god-touched street thief who can hear locks whisper. Pip tries to rob Freya, fails spectacularly when her charms burn his hands, and ends up owing her. She recruits him for the heist below. Emotional beat: wary humor; the found family begins assembling.

chapters.title: The Second Spoonful
chapters.summary: Freya's POV back at the palace. Her fellow taster Maren catches Freya smuggling out a ledger of the court's old bargains hidden in the royal kitchens. Instead of reporting her, Maren demands in. Emotional beat: trust tested and unexpectedly granted; loyalty vs. truth begins its argument.

chapters.title: Descent, With Receipts
chapters.summary: Full company POV rotation in one chapter—each character's voice as they enter the mountain's under-city, a market where souls are currency and memories are receipts. They locate Wren's contract but learn it can only be voided by an equivalent payment. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror at the price list.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Freya's POV before the court of the old gods. They offer her a bargain: keep her immunity and serve them as taster eternal, or surrender it and take Wren home mortal and unprotected. Meanwhile Pip discovers the court plans to use the reopened veil to reclaim the city above. Emotional beat: temptation laid bare.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Truth
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Back on the surface, the palace arrests Anselm as a heretic; Maren must choose between her oath and her new family. She burns the kitchen ledgers to destroy evidence against Freya, sacrificing her career. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizes—loyalty chosen over safe lies.

chapters.title: The Last Dish
chapters.summary: Climax. Freya's POV. She returns to the court and offers not her immunity but a final meal: every poison she has survived, brewed into one dish, eaten willingly—an act no immortal can match, since they cannot die. The court, bound by its own laws of exchange, must void Wren's contract. Freya collapses at death's door as the veil shudders. Emotional beat: sacrifice as answer.

chapters.title: Xanthe and the Veil Anew
chapters.summary: Resolution, rotating POV. Wren's soul, freed, chooses to pass on—but leaves Freya her name-day blessing. Freya wakes immune to nothing, alive anyway, because Pip's stolen luck and Maren's care kept her breathing. The city adjusts to living gods; Freya reopens her charm stall openly. Emotional beat: quiet joy; survival repaid by belonging.
